title: Power Automate: debug desktop flows using variable default values
summary: Hold for the licensing statement: Microsoft publishes licensing entitlements for local desktop-flow authoring and attended execution, so presenting licensing as unpublished overlooks the applicable platform rule. The documented designer controls, security warnings and roadmap facts otherwise check out.

claims.claim: Makers can assign a flow variable a default value in the Power Automate for desktop designer.
claims.quote: For each flow variable, you can: ... Define a default value and default data type used when starting a run with defaults.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn says sensitive input-variable defaults are not protected in action modals or the flow definition in Dataverse.
claims.quote: The default value of an input variable is visible in the creating or editing dialog when sensitivity is enabled. ... The default values aren't protected in the action modals and the flow definition in Dataverse.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Variable default values contribute to the desktop-flow definition saved in Dataverse with v2 schema.
claims.quote: The limit applies to the definition of the desktop flow saved in Dataverse, which can't exceed 16M characters. The issue can occur with a large desktop flow, such as when actions have large property values or variables have large default values.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Marking a flow variable as sensitive masks its value in the designer UI.
claims.quote: Mark as sensitive: Masks the variable value in the UI.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Learn describes sensitive-variable masking during debugging as basic protection against people looking at the developer's screen.
claims.quote: Masking sensitive variables during debugging provides only a basic form of protection to developers from third parties looking at their screens.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Learn's listed known issue says flows built or edited with version 2.14 or later cannot be opened or run with older desktop versions.
claims.quote: Flows built or edited with Power Automate for desktop version 2.14 or above are incompatible with older versions of Power Automate for desktop. You can't use older versions of Power Automate for desktop to open or run these flows.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Manage variables page itself names no licence, meter or charge for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate desktop flow variable default values debugging license premium free designer. Read Manage variables in full: no licence, meter or charge is named for the feature on that page.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The roadmap item states no licence or meter.
claims.quote: To use it, edit a variable in the designer and define a default value for debugging.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The applicable licensing model is unknown and whether a separate licence applies is Not yet published.
claims.quote: The Power Automate Free license includes creating and running cloud flows (without sharing), as well as authoring and running desktop flows locally (attended). Connector usage is limited to standard connectors only.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the unpublished-licensing statements and notes with: 'For local authoring and attended execution, Power Automate Free includes authoring and running desktop flows locally; connector usage is limited to standard connectors. Free users cannot share flows.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/power-automate-licensing/types and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/power-automate-licensing/deep-dive-on-specific-license#power-automate-free-license. Keep the narrower observation that the feature page names no separate licence or meter; do not extend Free entitlements to sharing or premium connectors.
